newsitem.title: CHINA: Two Tianjin futures firms suspended from trading.
newsitem.headline: Two Tianjin futures firms suspended from trading.

text.p: Two commodity firms in the north China city of Tianjin have been banned from doing futures business after lending out their seats on the Tianjin commodity exchange, the Shanghai Securities News said on Saturday.
The paper said Tianjin City Metals Materials Co. and Tianjin Commodities Group Co. had allowed other firms to use their places in the Tianjin United Futures exchange for the trading of red beans.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) ordered them to stop trading futures from Sept 16 and also strongly criticised the exchange for lax supervision.
The two companies must transfer all their contracts and clients to other companies within 20 trading days.
The paper said the exchange had not properly implemented trading rules, particularly with regard to the sourcing and movement of funds through the exchange.

"The exchange did not conduct effective supervision of abnormal behaviour by members, such as non-standard trading on their own account or operating non-standard agent arrangements," it said. "There were even cases of members privately transferring or lending out their seats (on the exchange)."

China's futures markets have come under ever-tighter supervision from the Beijing authorities who have indicated their determination to stamp out excessive speculation and non-approved trading practices.
